messages:
Dev Patel: First wave of quickstart template questions coming in from customers + community. Themes:
1) 429 handling (people think it’s a “bug” / don’t understand backoff vs retry storm)
2) streaming disconnects behind proxies (nginx / Cloudflare / corporate) esp. agents template
3) confusion about which timeout applies (client vs server vs proxy)

I pulled a few snippets from tickets + chat:
- “I get 429 right away even on small prompts; should I just retry immediately?”
- “Streaming works locally but disconnects in prod after ~60s.”
- “The template logs show ‘RateLimited’ but no guidance on what to do.”

Propose we ship doc updates + small template README changes ASAP.

SupportBot: :ticket: Related tickets: SUP-2949 (429 confusion), SUP-2934 (streaming disconnect behind proxy), SUP-2911 (RAG timeout on larger docs)

Owen Phillips: +1, seeing the same in escalations. The 429 behavior is biting people because they copy/paste a naive loop. Also a couple folks are missing that we return `Retry-After` sometimes.

Monica Patel: Re 429: the SDK helper defaults do exponential backoff + jitter + caps, but the templates might not be pointing people at it clearly. If someone isn’t using the helper and is doing manual fetch/axios they’re getting hammered.

Wei Chen: We can update docs site + template READMEs to be explicit:
- what 429 means (rate limit vs capacity)
- check headers (`Retry-After`, request id)
- recommended backoff snippet (language-specific)
- “don’t retry streaming mid-stream; restart from last stable point” guidance

Dana Lo: For TS template: we added basic 429 handler but it’s kinda hidden in `lib/client.ts`. People reading README don’t see it.

Ibrahim Khan: On streaming disconnects: most are proxies buffering SSE or closing idle connections. We should add a “if you are behind nginx, set these” section and also mention keep-alives.

Sean Gallagher: + from SRE side: we should explicitly say:
- set client timeout > expected generation time (or no timeout for SSE but enforce overall request budget)
- ensure proxy read timeout is high enough
- avoid infinite retries on 429/5xx; include max attempts and circuit breaker-ish behavior
Also we should tell folks to log the `x-redwood-request-id` so support can trace.

Dev Patel: Here are the concrete asks I’ve gotten this week:
- “Where do I configure retries/backoff?”
- “How can I see I’m being rate-limited vs a real error?”
- “Why does it work locally but not when deployed behind [proxy]?”

Monica Patel: For Python/TS SDKs:
- Recommend honoring `Retry-After` if present.
- For streaming: retry only on connect errors before receiving tokens; after stream starts, don’t auto-resume unless app supports it.
I can draft a snippet for both and send to Docs.

Wei Chen: I’ll take a docs patch:
1) Add a “Handling 429s (rate limits)” callout in each template guide
2) Add “Streaming behind proxies” troubleshooting
3) Add a short “Common misconfigs” section: missing API key, wrong region/model combo, too-low timeouts

Dana Lo: I can update the TS template README to link directly to the retry helper + show an example with `maxRetries` and `timeoutMs`.

Ibrahim Khan: Python template: we should ensure the default timeout is not overly aggressive for RAG queries when retrieval adds latency. SUP-2911 sounded like larger docs -> longer retrieval -> client times out.

Sean Gallagher: For 429 guidance, can we include a one-liner about “429 != error in the model; it’s backpressure; treat it as expected under load” + suggest using Dedicated if they need predictable throughput.

Owen Phillips: Yes please. Support messaging: “If your workload needs sustained throughput, Dedicated capacity avoids noisy-neighbor behavior.” But keep it non-salesy.

Dev Patel: Streaming/proxy specifics I’ve seen:
- nginx default `proxy_read_timeout 60s` => stream dies at 60s
- buffering enabled => chunks don’t flush
- some corporate proxies kill long-lived connections
We should include a minimal nginx config snippet.

Wei Chen: Proposed snippet (happy to adjust):
```nginx
location / {
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
}
```
And mention Cloudflare: disable response buffering / increase limits if applicable.

Monica Patel: Also mention setting `Accept: text/event-stream` for SSE and not using libraries that buffer by default.

Dana Lo: +1. In Node, some folks run behind Next/Express and forget to disable compression for SSE. If we see it a lot, we can add a “don’t gzip SSE” note.

Sean Gallagher: On retries: please include max attempts and overall budget. Something like:
- retryable: 429, 408, 409 (idempotent only), 5xx
- non-retryable: 4xx (except above)
- cap attempts (e.g., 5)
- max backoff (e.g., 30s)

Ibrahim Khan: Re idempotency: if they’re doing ingestion jobs, we should mention idempotency keys / dedupe so retries don’t duplicate work.

Wei Chen: Action items I’m hearing:
- Monica: provide SDK helper snippet + recommended defaults text
- Dana: update TS template README (surface retries/timeouts + streaming note)
- Ibra: sanity check Python template timeout defaults for RAG paths
- Wei (me): docs site troubleshooting page update
- Dev/Owen: compile top Qs into a short Support macro for 429 + streaming

Dev Patel: Works. I’ll draft the support macro:
- Ask for `x-redwood-request-id`
- Confirm whether streaming or non-streaming
- Confirm deployment (proxy / load balancer)
- Link to new docs sections once merged

Owen Phillips: Please also add one line: “If you see repeated 429s, check your concurrency + token rate; templates default to safe concurrency but your deployment may override.”

Monica Patel: I’ll send snippets in ~1h. Also I’d like to add explicit logging when 429 happens: include retry delay + attempt number (without spamming). We already do that in SDK but templates should show it.

Wei Chen: Great—once I have snippets I’ll open a docs PR and link back here. :thumbsup:

Sean Gallagher: If you want SRE eyes on the wording (avoid encouraging retry storms), ping me before publish.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: Will do. I’ll update this thread with macro text + which tickets it covers once ready.
